comments.author: wdower
comments.text:
Architectural Decisions from 2026-01-03 discussion:

DECISION: Dual implementation strategy (TypeScript + Go)
- TypeScript: hdf-converters npm package for programmatic use, web apps
- Go: Native converters in hdf-cli for security, distribution, performance
- No viable TypeScript-to-Go transpiler exists (researched: leona/ts2go, armsnyder/ts2go, CodeConvert.ai - all insufficient)
- Manual porting required but manageable (~500 LOC per converter)

RATIONALE - Security:
- Eliminate Node.js runtime attack surface (~30MB + npm ecosystem)
- No npm supply chain vulnerabilities
- Smaller trusted computing base (~2-5MB Go vs ~30-50MB Node.js)
- Static analysis, memory safety, easier auditing
- Single binary distribution (no runtime dependencies)

RATIONALE - User Experience:
- No Node.js installation required for hdf-cli users
- Faster startup (~1-5ms vs ~50-200ms)
- Single binary, smaller download size

MAINTENANCE STRATEGY:
- Differential testing ensures parity (this framework)
- Shared test fixtures (single source of truth)
- TypeScript as reference implementation, Go ports once stable
- ~30 converters needed eventually (from SAF CLI parity)
- Estimated: TypeScript first (~4hr), Go port (~6hr), testing (~2hr) = ~12hr per converter
- Differential testing reduces unit test duplication by ~40%

CLI PATTERN DECISION:
- Pattern: 'hdf convert <src-format> to <dest-format> <input> [output]'
- Explicit and readable, supports bidirectional (HDF to other formats)
- Examples:
  - hdf convert v1 to v2 scan.json
  - hdf convert burpsuite to hdf scan.xml results.json
  - hdf convert hdf to sarif results.json output.sarif

title: Add omitempty tags to Go type generation for discriminated unions
description:
Fix Go JSON output to match schema discriminated union intent by adding omitempty tags to optional fields.

Problem:
- Target uses oneOf discriminated union (Host, Container, Cloud, etc.)
- quicktype generates single Go struct with all union fields
- Without omitempty, Go marshals all nil fields as null
- Result: Host target outputs 37 fields (35 nulls) instead of 7 relevant fields

Solution:
- Update hdf-schema type generation to add omitempty tags to optional fields
- Ensures only populated fields appear in JSON output
- Matches schema semantic intent of discriminated unions

Approach (TDD):
1. Write test that asserts omitempty tags exist on generated types
2. Write test that validates marshaled JSON only contains non-null fields
3. Update quicktype generation or post-processing to add omitempty
4. Verify all converters produce cleaner output

Affects:
- hdf-schema/src/generators/go.ts (type generation)
- All converters using Target, EvaluatedBaseline, etc.
- Should be backward compatible (omitting nulls does not break consumers)

close_reason: Added XMLValidator check to parseXmlWithArrays() for consistency with parseXml(). Throws descriptive error on malformed XML. Added test case. All 47 XML tests passing.

title: Implement HDF-to-XML converter
description: Create converter to export HDF JSON to XML format. Design XML schema that preserves HDF structure: baselines, targets, requirements hierarchy. Use buildXml() utility. Consider two formats: (1) Generic XML representation of HDF structure, (2) XCCDF-compatible output for interoperability. Include TypeScript and Go implementations with differential testing. Useful for tools that require XML input or legacy system integration.
